corrections.why: Sparta never joined the League of Corinth (337 BC) and was neither conquered nor garrisoned by Philip or Alexander; it remained fully independent and hostile. Folding PEL into the 'macedon' entity's regions directly contradicts that same entity's own note ('League of Corinth behind him (Sparta aloof)'). Consistent with how the file already treats PEL at -359 and -301 (merged into greek_poleis rather than a Macedonian possession).

macedon.note: League of Corinth behind him; Sparta stays out, unconquered, Alexander invades Asia

greek_poleis.note: Sparta and the Peloponnese stand apart from Alexander's league

corrections.why: Sparta remained un-conquered and outside Macedonian control for the whole of Alexander's reign, took no part in his campaigns, and sits out the Lamian War that erupts this same year. PEL should not sit inside the Macedon/'Empire of Alexander' bloc at his death.

greek_poleis.note: Sparta and the free poleis sit out the Lamian War against Macedon

corrections.why: After Ipsus (301 BC), Ariarathes II recovered Cappadocia that same year, killing the Macedonian/Lysimachan satrap Amyntas, and ruled as a semi-independent king under Seleucid protection - Cappadocia was not part of Lysimachus's kingdom at -301. (Its Pontic hinterland, PON, is kept with it per the file's own -323 approximation for the same dynasty.)

addEntities.name: Cappadocia (Ariarathes II)
addEntities.note: Ariarathes II retakes Cappadocia after Ipsus, slaying satrap Amyntas; rules under Seleucid protection

lysimachus.note: Thrace and western Anatolia won at Ipsus; Cappadocia stays with Ariarathes II

verified: Persia's Egyptian loss to Amyrtaeus (28th Dynasty, founded -404) and recovery attempts through -359 (30th Dynasty, Nectanebo II) track the historical timeline correctly.
Archaeanactid Bosporus (CRM held by greek_poleis) from -480, superseded by the Spartocid Bosporan Kingdom founded -438 - both hand-offs land on the right slice years.
Teres I founding the Odrysian Kingdom at -480, entity introduced at -431, matches conventional dating.
Rhodes' synoikism founding date -408 is correct and the entity appears from -400 onward.

Carthage's absorption of Sardinia and Tartessos-successor Andalusia by -500 (post-Alalia, post-Tartessos collapse) is broadly right and already flagged by the author as a region-resolution approximation in uncertainties.
Cyprus tributary to Saite Egypt under Amasis II at -550, then folded into the Achaemenid empire from -500, matches Herodotus and the conquest sequence.
Rome's founding date -509 and its steady territorial growth through the Latin War (-338), First/Second Samnite Wars are placed on plausible years.
Cappadocia under Ariarathes I, 'never subdued by Alexander,' at -323 is correct and was the detail that flagged the -301 error.

sources.title: Why Didn't Alexander the Great Conquer Sparta? - neutralhistory.com

uncertainties: Kept PON bundled with CAP under the restored Ariarathes II at -301 for consistency with the file's own -323 approximation, though Pontus proper (Mithridates I Ktistes, founded -281 per the canon) is not really Cappadocian territory - the region likely had no firm central authority at -301.

Did not disturb the file's existing PEL-as-part-of-greek_poleis treatment at -359/-301 (already flagged in the original uncertainties); only corrected the two intervening slices where PEL was inconsistently folded into Macedon.
